status_summary: No charter that removes activity restrictions in exchange for higher equity or risk retention was found. The new licensing paths created since 2025 run the other way on activities: the GENIUS Act (Public Law 119-27, signed 2025-07-18) set up a federal framework for payment stablecoin issuers with capital, liquidity and reserve requirements, and the OCC's proposal of 2026-03-02 confined approved issuers to stablecoin issuance, redemption, reserve management, custody and directly supporting activities. The OCC finalized that framework on 2026-10-23 (91 FR 67000, effective 2027-01-18) with permitted and prohibited activity provisions and capital requirements, so it remains a narrow, single-purpose license rather than the general charter the text describes.

timeline.event: The GENIUS Act (S. 1582) becomes Public Law 119-27, creating a federal framework for payment stablecoin issuers with capital, liquidity and reserve requirements (per the bill status summary). Listed as a parallel, not as progress.

The OCC proposes rules implementing the GENIUS Act for issuers under its jurisdiction, confining approved issuers to stablecoin-related activities and setting minimum capital requirements. Listed as a parallel, not as progress.

The OCC publishes its final rule implementing the GENIUS Act for payment stablecoin issuers under its jurisdiction (91 FR 67000, RIN 1557-AF41, effective 2027-01-18), adding 12 CFR part 15 with permitted and prohibited activity provisions, reserve, redemption, custody and application rules, and capital and operational backstop requirements. Listed as a parallel, not as progress.

title: Create new financial charters with fewer activity limits for higher equity standards
uncertainties: No charter that removes activity restrictions in return for higher equity or risk retention was found. The GENIUS Act and the OCC's 2026 proposal create a narrow stablecoin license, and the March 2026 OCC chartering rule widens activity for trust-limited national banks without a capital trade; both are treated as adjacent. The OCC newsroom could not be read, and reported conditional trust charter approvals of 2025-12-12 were not confirmed from the OCC. The Unified Agenda rule lists on reginfo.gov for Treasury (including the OCC), the FDIC and the NCUA (headed 'Agency Rule List - 2026') list licensing and de novo chartering procedure changes and no new charter type. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19. The OCC final rule of 2026-10-23 was read on the Federal Register only in part: the preamble confirms sections on permitted activities, prohibited activities and capital, but the regulatory text of those sections fell beyond the portion read, so the claim that the final rule keeps issuers to stablecoin activities rests on the proposal and the preamble.
